newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU meeting on Zaire crisis planned for November 7.
newsitem.headline: EU meeting on Zaire crisis planned for November 7.

text.p: European Union ministers have been invited to meet in Brussels next Thursday to discuss emergency humanitarian support for more than a million refugees caught in fighting in Eastern Zaire, current EU president Ireland said.

Joan Burton, minister of state at Ireland's Department of Foreign Affairs, said in a statement on Friday she had called the meeting at the request of Belgium, former colonial power of the central African country.
Hundreds of thousands of Burundian and Rwandan refugees have fled camps in Eastern Zaire because of fighting between Zairean troops and Tutsi rebels.

"A coordinated and effective response by the Union and its member states is vital...as several hundred thousand civilians are in grave danger of death, injury or illness from either violence or lack of food and shelter," Burton said in her letter of invitation to the meeting.
She said the meeting was an "essential complement to the ongoing political efforts to bring about a ceasefire and to establish stability in the region".

Ireland said member states had been asked to provide details of actions undertaken or planned to help alleviate the crisis, and the European Commission was to report to the meeting on its assessment of the humanitarian situation and its plans for a response.
